mixed4b:431.real_s1: The unit responds to furry mammal heads, mainly dogs, when they are shown face-on at a medium framing, with the furry ears and the neck/shoulder region next to the face clearly in view. It responds more weakly to other furry mammals with a similar head-and-neck fur layout.
mixed4b:431.real_s2: The unit responds to framed, frontal views of furry mammal heads (mostly dogs) where the head, furry ears and the neck/shoulder region beside the face are clearly visible, with the animal at a medium scale (about a quarter to half of the image). It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar head/fur structure.
mixed4b:431.real_s3: The unit responds to the head and neck/shoulder region of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is strongest when the head is seen from the front and fills a moderate share of the frame (between a quarter and half of the image) with furry ears and the neck area clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.
mixed4b:431.null_s1: The unit responds mainly to dogs and dog-like canids, with weaker responses to other furry mammals such as meerkats. The claimed focus on the fur beside the face is not supported; it seems to respond to dog-ness as a whole.
mixed4b:431.null_s2: The unit responds mainly to dogs, especially photos where the dog's neck/shoulder area beside the face and its furry ears are clearly visible. It responds less, or at most weakly, to other furry mammals.
mixed4b:431.null_s3: The unit responds mainly to dogs (and dog-like canids such as wolves), with weaker activity for other furry mammals like meerkats; it is not tuned to a specific head part, fur length or view.

mixed4b:443.real_s1: The unit responds to frontal, camera-facing furry animal faces with both eyes clearly visible, mostly dog faces in these photos, and extends to other furry mammal faces such as the lesser panda.
mixed4b:443.real_s2: The unit responds to frontal, camera-facing faces of dogs (and other furry mammals) where both eyes are clearly visible, peaking on a single, reasonably large face with an unobstructed eye/brow region. It extends more weakly to other furry mammal faces such as the lesser panda.
mixed4b:443.real_s3: The unit responds to frontal, upright canine faces with both eyes and the eye/brow region fully in view, at moderate-to-large scale. It extends more weakly to frontal faces of other furry mammals such as the lesser panda, not only to wild canids.
mixed4b:443.null_s1: The unit responds to dog breeds and closely related animals (including the red panda), driven mainly by class identity rather than by face details within those classes, with perhaps a mild preference for three-quarter views of the face.
mixed4b:443.null_s2: The unit responds mainly to dogs at the class level, especially many dog breeds plus a related furry mammal (lesser panda). Within those classes, the specific face-related properties claimed (upright face, eye/upper-face region) do not explain its activity.
mixed4b:443.null_s3: The unit responds broadly to dogs, especially small long-haired terriers, toy breeds and spitz/shepherd types, and extends weakly to a dog-like furry face, the lesser panda. It does not appear to respond specifically to the frontal eye/brow region.

mixed4b:429.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, frontal dog face in which both eyes and the nose/muzzle can be seen, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.
mixed4b:429.real_s2: The unit responds to clearly visible, upright, roughly frontal dog faces where both eyes and the nose/muzzle are in view, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.
mixed4b:429.real_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, roughly frontal dog face, with eyes and muzzle both in view, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.
mixed4b:429.null_s1: The unit responds to dog faces, especially large, clearly visible ones in non-canonical poses (tilted sideways or three-quarter view), rather than specifically to upright frontal faces. Tan or golden coats get a slightly stronger response.
mixed4b:429.null_s2: The unit responds to dog faces that are large in the frame, and it is especially strong when the head is tilted or in three-quarter view rather than upright and frontal. Tan or golden coats may add a little to the response.
mixed4b:429.null_s3: The unit responds to dog faces, most strongly when the face is large in the frame and the head is tilted sideways or turned to a three-quarter view, rather than upright and head-on.

mixed4d:409.real_s1: The unit responds to horizontally elongated bodies clearly raised on legs or wheels, seen at an angle that shows the side, which in practice means mostly road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks) seen in three-quarter or side view. It probably extends to standing quadrupeds as the original explanation claims, but these photos cannot test that.
mixed4d:409.real_s2: The unit responds to the long body of a road vehicle seen raised on its wheels, best from a three-quarter or side view that shows the side and front wheel. The claimed dog-torso response is not supported by this data.
mixed4d:409.real_s3: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body visibly raised on legs or wheels, seen from the side or at a three-quarter angle. Mainly this is the body of a road vehicle above its wheels, with a related extension to the flanks of standing four-legged animals such as dogs.
mixed4d:409.null_s1: The unit responds mainly to motor vehicles (cars, vans, trucks), especially a raised, elongated body over its wheels seen at a three-quarter or partial-side angle with the front wheel visible. It extends more weakly to similar shapes such as an airliner on its landing gear and car grilles; the claimed preference for dogs and quadrupeds is not supported.
mixed4d:409.null_s2: The unit mainly responds to the lower side of road vehicles: a partial side view showing the front wheel and the elongated body raised on its wheels. It extends more weakly to other long objects on wheels, such as airliners, and to vehicle fronts like grilles.
mixed4d:409.null_s3: The unit mainly responds to the body of a road vehicle seen from the side or at three-quarters, raised on visible wheels, with the front wheel in view. Its weaker response to the flanks of standing quadrupeds (dogs, a weasel) looks like an extension of the same 'long body on supports' shape.

mixed4b:237.real_s1: The unit responds to clearly visible, well-defined side door windows (glass plus frame and pillars) of real, upright road vehicles, especially the front cab or driver window seen in a three-quarter view, with pickups and vans favored slightly.
mixed4b:237.real_s2: The unit responds to the side door-window area of real, upright road vehicles: the door glass with a clearly defined frame and pillars, mostly the front cab/driver window, seen from a front or rear three-quarter angle.
mixed4b:237.real_s3: The unit responds to the framed side door window of a real, upright road vehicle (glass pane with clearly defined frame and pillars), best seen in front or rear three-quarter view.
mixed4b:237.null_s1: The unit responds to clearly framed side windows of road vehicles, meaning door glass with distinct frames and pillars, most strongly on larger vehicles such as truck cabs and buses. It also responds somewhat more to toy, model or drawn vehicles than to real ones.
mixed4b:237.null_s2: The unit responds to the clearly delineated side-window region of a vehicle: door glass bounded by a visible frame and pillars, most often the front cab/driver door window. It extends somewhat to rear passenger or cargo windows and to boxier vehicles such as trucks and buses.
mixed4b:237.null_s3: The unit responds to clearly framed side door windows of road vehicles: glass panes with distinct frames and pillars, seen from the side rather than through the windshield or rear window. The response is somewhat stronger for larger vehicles such as trucks and buses and for non-photographic renderings such as toys and models.

mixed4b:373.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible road-vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch or fender, seen at medium scale from a side or three-quarter angle, especially the front wheel of vans, buses and trucks.
mixed4b:373.real_s2: The unit responds to a clearly visible road-vehicle wheel sitting in its wheel arch, seen from the side or a three-quarter angle at medium scale, and it fires most for the front wheel. It responds weakly or not at all when the wheel is small, hidden, seen head-on, or has no arch around it.
mixed4b:373.real_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, medium-sized wheel of a road vehicle sitting inside its wheel arch, seen from the side or at an angle, with a preference for the front wheel. The vehicle type does not matter much.
mixed4b:373.null_s1: The unit responds to clearly visible road-vehicle wheels seen from the side so they look round, regardless of vehicle type; the surrounding wheel arch does not appear to matter.
mixed4b:373.null_s2: The unit responds to a clearly visible, round vehicle wheel seen from the side, most often a front wheel; it does not need the surrounding wheel arch.
mixed4b:373.null_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, round vehicle wheel seen from the side (side profile of the vehicle), on any kind of road vehicle; the wheel arch or fender does not appear to matter.

mixed4e:55.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, front-facing muzzle of a furry mammal (nose, whisker pad, mouth, often light-furred with visible whiskers), regardless of species. It gives weaker, related responses to face-like fronts such as car grilles.
mixed4e:55.real_s2: Responds to a clearly visible, upright, camera-facing muzzle region (nose, mouth, whisker pad, often lighter fur) of a furry mammal, regardless of species. A car front/grille gives at most a weak, face-like extension.
mixed4e:55.real_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, camera-facing muzzle of a furry mammal (nose, mouth, whisker pad, often light fur below the eyes), regardless of species. It gives a weaker, related response to face-like frontal structures such as car grilles.
mixed4e:55.null_s1: The unit responds mainly to the faces of small to medium furry mammals (foxes, red pandas, lynxes and cats, with weasels and hamsters), seen at moderate size, often partly hidden or tilted. It extends more weakly to face-like car fronts and grilles.
mixed4e:55.null_s2: The unit responds broadly to small-to-moderate, often partly hidden or tilted faces of furry mammals, most strongly fox and red panda, with weaker extension to car fronts and grilles. It does not appear to respond specifically to a clearly visible muzzle.
mixed4e:55.null_s3: The unit responds mainly to furry mammal faces, especially small carnivore-like faces such as wild cats, foxes, red pandas, weasels, house cats and hamsters, and more weakly to face-like car fronts and grilles. It is not specifically tuned to a clear, close-up muzzle with whiskers.

mixed5a:719.real_s1: The unit responds mainly to close-up, frame-filling views of compact man-made or handmade objects, regardless of whether they have curved contours. A weaker related preference is for ornamental surface patterns such as radial, floral or petal designs on those objects.
mixed5a:719.real_s2: The unit responds mainly to close-up, frame-filling man-made or handcrafted objects, such as shoes, wallets, stockings and trinkets. Within those, it responds somewhat more when the surface carries decorative curved, radial or floral patterns rather than only a plain curved outline.
mixed5a:719.real_s3: The unit mainly responds to a close-up of a compact man-made or handmade object that fills much of the frame, not to curved contours as such. It responds somewhat more when the surface carries ornamental radial, floral or patterned decoration.
mixed5a:719.null_s1: The unit mainly responds to curved outline contours of compact man-made objects (e.g., the rounded edge of a shoe, wallet or mouse) that stand out only moderately from their background. The proposed extension to decorative radial or petal patterns is not supported.
mixed5a:719.null_s2: The unit responds mainly to the curved outline of a man-made object (e.g., the edge of a shoe, pouch or mouse) seen at moderate contrast against its background. It responds less to curves that come from decorative surface patterns, and less when the object is starkly separated from the background.
mixed5a:719.null_s3: The unit responds to the outline of compact, close-up man-made objects such as leather goods, shoes, erasers, sharpeners and ocarinas, especially when the object sits against a background of only moderate contrast. It does not respond to radial or floral decorative patterns on surfaces.
